title: All 11 sectors rise as the S&P 500 caps a 5.6% week
summary: The Nasdaq Composite gained 2.3% as chip stocks rebounded after Thanksgiving. Small caps also beat the S&P 500, and every S&P sector finished higher at Friday’s early close.
close: At the 1 p.m. New York close, the S&P 500 stood at 7,297.49, up 1.60%, and the Nasdaq Composite reached 24,129.50, up 2.3%. The Dow added 591.99 points to 50,774.94. The Russell 2000 gained 1.71% to 2,750.30, extending its weekly advance to 6.5%. The Cboe VIX spot index ended at 23.81, below Wednesday’s 28.29.
drivers: Technology led all eleven sectors with a 2.8% gain. Broadcom rose 3.8% and Micron gained 7.6%, while Amazon’s roughly 4% rise contributed an estimated 11 points to the S&P 500. The start of holiday shopping gave investors a first look at demand. Adobe Analytics put Thanksgiving Day online spending at about $7.1 billion, up 10.4% from a year earlier. Retail shares still diverged, with Macy’s rising and Target edging lower.
review: Wednesday’s outlook called for the rebound to survive if small caps held 2,684.94. Friday met that test and both conditions for a broader recovery. The Russell cleared 2,704.06 and the S&P 500 cleared 7,237.17, finishing well above the 7,073.78 downside threshold.
outlook: For Monday, November 30, the question is whether Friday’s broad buying survives a full trading day. If the S&P 500 holds 7,237.17, the base case is that large caps retain their breakout. A close above Friday’s 7,297.49 alongside a Russell 2000 close above 2,750.30 would confirm that both groups are extending the advance. An S&P 500 close below 7,237.17 would invalidate the breakout call even if small caps continue to rise.

title: Eight sectors rise as the S&P 500 nearly erases a 3.2% slide
summary: The S&P 500 ended just 0.25% lower after falling as much as 3.2% on Wednesday. Small caps and the Dow finished higher, while losses in Nvidia and other large technology names kept the Nasdaq in the red.
close: The S&P 500 closed at 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.62% to 23,585.80. The Dow gained 0.33% to 50,182.95 and the Russell 2000 rose 0.71% to 2,704.06. Eight of the S&P 500’s eleven sectors advanced. Despite that breadth and the recovery from the morning low, the Cboe VIX closed at 28.29, up 1.93 points from Tuesday.
drivers: Nvidia fell 3.91%, subtracting an estimated 17.1 points from the S&P 500. That one stock accounted for nearly all of the index’s net 18.31-point loss, even as other stocks gained ground. Investors also had fresh inflation data to weigh before Thanksgiving. The Bureau of Economic Analysis reported that October consumer prices, measured by the PCE index, rose 0.3% for the month and 3.8% from a year earlier.
review: Tuesday’s outlook was partly confirmed. The Russell cleared the 2,684.94 threshold, but the S&P 500 finished below the 7,237.17 needed to confirm that large caps were participating too. Its close remained above 7,073.78, so the stated downside condition was never triggered on a closing basis.
outlook: After Thursday’s Thanksgiving closure, the next session is Friday, November 27, with equities closing at 1 p.m. New York time. If small caps hold Tuesday’s 2,684.94 level, the base case is for the week’s rebound to survive the shortened session. A Russell close above 2,704.06 together with an S&P 500 close above 7,237.17 would confirm a broader recovery. An S&P 500 close below 7,073.78 would invalidate that view.

title: Nasdaq gives back 1.5% as Nvidia slides and small caps advance
summary: The S&P 500 kept nearly nine-tenths of Monday’s gain as selling in AI stocks pulled the Nasdaq lower. The Dow and Russell 2000 rose, although decliners narrowly outnumbered gainers on both major exchanges.
close: The S&P 500 ended Tuesday at 7,201.09, down 0.50%, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54. The Dow added 423.39 points to finish at 50,018.70, while the Russell 2000 gained 15.29 points to 2,684.94. The Cboe Volatility Index closed at 26.36, down 0.26 point. On the NYSE, roughly 104 issues fell for every 100 that rose. On Nasdaq, 2,548 fell and 2,376 rose.
drivers: Nvidia fell 5.9% a day after Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive sparked a rally in chip stocks. Anthropic also slipped below its IPO price. Earnings gave retailers a different cue. Abercrombie & Fitch raised its full-year profit forecast and its shares climbed 19.7%. Health care posted the strongest gain among the S&P 500 sectors.
review: Tuesday’s close met both conditions in Monday’s outlook. The Russell 2000 finished above 2,669.66 and the VIX ended below 26.62. The S&P 500 gave back just 36.08 points of Monday’s 326.78-point rise, leaving it well above the 7,073.78 level that would have invalidated the call.
outlook: For Wednesday, November 25, the base case is that small caps help sustain this week’s rebound if technology selling stays contained. A Russell 2000 close above Tuesday’s 2,684.94 alongside an S&P 500 close above Monday’s 7,237.17 would confirm that buyers are making headway in both groups. An S&P 500 close below 7,073.78 would erase more than half of Monday’s gain and invalidate the rebound outlook.

title: Nvidia powers a 6.5% Nasdaq rebound as small caps join the rally
summary: The S&P 500 broke a seven-session losing streak, and Nvidia alone accounted for about a third of its gain. Smaller companies also rallied, giving Tuesday’s session a useful test of how far the recovery can spread.
close: The S&P 500 finished Monday at 7,237.17, up 4.73%, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 6.51% to 24,089.56. The Russell 2000 added 3.40% to 2,669.66. The Cboe Volatility Index ended at 26.62 in the daily index series, down 9.27 points from Friday’s 35.89. Options traders were pricing in smaller swings over the coming month even as stocks posted an unusually large one-day move.
drivers: Stock futures were already rising before Nvidia announced that its board had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. The news gave the rebound a clear leader. Nvidia rose 31.48% and contributed an estimated 111 points to the S&P 500’s 327-point advance. Micron gained 19.04%, while Exxon Mobil and Chevron both fell. The small-cap advance shows buying reached beyond chipmakers, even though the largest technology companies supplied much of the index gain.
outlook: For Tuesday, November 24, the base case is that the market holds most of Monday’s rebound. A Russell 2000 close above 2,669.66 alongside a VIX close below 26.62 would confirm that smaller companies are still drawing buyers as expected volatility eases. An S&P 500 close below 7,073.78 would erase more than half of Monday’s point gain and invalidate that outlook.
